title: Deployment Handoff Playbook — Staffing & Triage Notes (Jun 24 2026)
content:
Context:
This is a working notes doc from the June 24 triage/sync where we reworked the handoff playbook between Solutions Engineering (SE) and Field Ops for Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-successful-serve and cut the number of re-opened incidents caused by late-discovered network and certificate issues.

Summary of problems observed (past 8 installs):
- Recurrent blocker class A: customer network MTU and firewall rules not validated before image boot — caused KV cache warmup failures and long tail latency (3 installs).
- Recurrent blocker class B: cert chain mismatch due to pre-existing internal PKI; our automated CA pinning step failed (2 installs).
- Hand-off friction: SE left ambiguous owner for preflight network call; Field Ops discovered infra gaps only during on-site cmdline debug.
- Staffing gap: weekend on-call coverage for installs with custom network routing not clearly assigned; two installs had 12–18 hour waits for netops responses.

Decisions / playbook changes agreed today:
1) New "Early Network Validation" call to be scheduled at least 72 hours before target install window. Attendees: customer netops, SE lead, Field Ops engineer. Mandatory checklist to cover: BGP/peering expectations, MTU, egress NAT, port 22/443 + ephemeral ports, IDS/IPS rules, and ICMP reachability for internal subnets.

2) Preflight automation: add an "edge-network-check" script to the public deploy-scripts repo. Script will run from a cloud VM and validate: TCP/UDP handshakes to the customer-provided endpoints, MTU probe, TLS handshake verification against chain provided by customer, and a basic DNS resolution sweep. Output will be a machine-readable JSON and a human summary.

3) Certificate policy: if customer PKI is present, require SE to submit cert chain and test cert via the new script. If mismatch detected, escalate to "PKI bridge" flow (Confluence-12345) rather than on-site fiddling.

4) On-call staffing change: create a 72‑hour install window owner rotation. Field Ops will roster a single point-of-contact per install (POC) and SE will roster a backup. On weekends, at least one engineer must be cross-trained for network debugging (see training checklist).

5) Standard escalation matrix: POC -> Field Ops EM -> SRE on-call -> Engineering manager -> Customer success engagement. Include explicit SLAs for response times during the install window (15m ack, 60m triage).

Action items (owner — due):
- Marco Diaz — add "edge-network-check" script to infra repo with docs and sample output (due 2026-07-02). Linked PR: git://infra/deploy-scripts#12.
- Priya Nair — update SE playbook steps to require cert chain upload and preflight call scheduling; add email template for scheduling (due 2026-06-30).
- Samir Gupta — draft weekend cross-training plan and run first 1-hour session on 2026-07-05 (due 2026-07-05).
- Evelyn Chen — update customer-facing runbook and publish Confluence-12345 pointer in the playbook (due 2026-06-28).
- Field Ops (rotation) — trial the 72‑hr POC rotation on the next two installs and report metrics (time-to-first-resolve, number of reopens) by 2026-07-15.

Triage matrix (quick reference):
- Network connectivity failing (ping/tcp timeout): run edge-network-check; if failures persist, escalate to customer netops, provide packet capture template. Severity P0 if customer production SLA impacted.
- TLS handshake error / cert chain mismatch: check uploaded chain vs presented certs. If custom CA, follow PKI bridge flow.
- Disk or NFS mount errors on node: check kernel logs, verify NFS server versions and firewall rules for NFS ports. Assign to Field Ops.
- GPU node not visible / NVidia drivers mismatch: check node OS image digest, compare to expected (runtime image 1.8.2); if mismatch, roll node to known-good image.

Checklist excerpt for "Early Network Validation" call:
- Confirm network lead and escalation contact (name, phone, calendar).
- Confirm subnets and CIDR ranges for peering.
- Confirm MTU and fragmentation policy.
- Confirm outbound egress rules and IPs used by Redwood runtime (list of IPs or NAT ranges).
- Confirm TLS/PKI expectations and provide cert chain if using custom CA.
- Confirm whether port 22 access will be allowed for debugging or if a bastion will be used (provide bastion creds ticket).

Notes from today's customer examples:
- Customer A (large fintech): prevented a 2‑day delay after we required an early network validation call; found MPLS MTU set to 1400 (ours expects 1500) — temporary workaround applied on the path, permanent fix scheduled. Ticket: JIRA-PDEP-4821.
- Customer B (regional healthcare): PKI conflict — their internal CA re‑signs leaf certs. We moved to PKI bridge flow and used TLS proxy to avoid on-site cert installs. Customer now reviewing HSM/KMS integration options. Ticket: JIRA-PDEP-4899.

Risks / open questions:
- Some customers refuse to allow port 22; we need a standard secure debug proxy with short-lived creds. Who owns building that? (TBD — suggested: Platform Eng).
- Will the edge-network-check be sufficient for complex routed setups (GRE, VXLAN)? Consider adding optional advanced checks or manual network design review for customers with complex overlays.
- Staffing: we need to ensure rotation doesn't overload Field Ops. Monitoring of load and hiring plan to be discussed with Eng Ops.

Metrics to track (start now):
- Time from SE send to first successful network validation (target <72h).
- Number of installs reopened due to network or cert bugs (target reduce by 50% quarter-over-quarter).
- Median time-to-fix for P0 install incidents (target <4h during install window).

Appendix (quick templates):
- Preflight email template: condensed lines for customer calendar invite and required artifacts (subnets, cert chain, netops contact).
- Packet-capture upload instructions: standard tcpdump flags, redaction checklist for PHI.

Next sync: 2026-07-01 — 30m to review progress on actions and iterate on the playbook.

Raw notes / thoughts (scratch):
- Consider building a small web form for customers to upload cert chain and network topology diagrams before the call. Could be integrated with the onboarding flow.
- Explore an "install rehearsal" with the runtime in a staging VPC mirrored to the customer's expected CIDR—helpful for complex NAT/peering scenarios.
- We should maintain a short list of approved on-site tooling binaries (diagnostic bundle) and their hashes to avoid ad-hoc downloads.

Document history: created by Evelyn Chen in triage sync; edits by Marco and Priya on 2026-06-25; will be folded into Confluence-12345 once action items are implemented.
